thread:
Maya: heads-up — we've got a sustained p95 latency spike on prod around 09:42 UTC, looks tenant-localized. Route /v1/generate shows 2-3x latency for a handful of requests :eyes:
Oliver: saw that in alerts, is it KV-cache related or batching? any noisy tenant?
Maya: initial drilldown: big prompt-length variance + tool-calling loop from that tenant. suspect prefetcher + kernel selection oscillation when sequence lengths jump. stack traces attached in perf-bot message below.
perf-bot: quick summary: flame and trace linked -> https://perf.internal/trace/1867504321 (perm: eng-runtime)
Cheng: flame snippet from the trace (tail):
```
-- time(ms) --
kernel_select()         120ms
continuous_batcher()    95ms
kv_cache::lookup()      60ms
kv_cache::evict()       40ms
dispatch_tool_call()    180ms
```
Cheng: tool loop shows repeated dispatches that bypassed prefix caching, causing KV churn and kernel_choice to flip between small-seq and long-seq optimized kernels
Sarah: confirmation from node logs: repeated cache misses with eviction pressure on gpu-6, see log fragment:
```
[09:42:10] tenant=acme-tooling prompt_len=3200 kernel_hint=long_seq
[09:42:10] kvcache_lookup miss key=prefix:acme:123
[09:42:10] kvcache_evict key=prefix:acme:98 size=1.2MB
[09:42:11] kernel_select switching to small_seq (latency expected lower)
[09:42:11] kernel_select switching to long_seq (hot path)
```
Aisha: so the prefetcher sized for steady-state long prompts but the tenant had a burst of short tool calls nested inside long contexts. That pattern makes batching heuristics pick incompatible kernels and prevents prefix reuse.
Maya: mitigation proposal: 1) throttle tenant concurrency at router to cap in-flight streams 2) route tenant to model-variant with fixed-kernel policy (force long_seq) 3) push a kvcache retention tweak to reduce premature eviction for this tenant
Oliver: can we do (1) and (2) now? I can apply a routing rule and a temporary quota.
deploy-bot: ran: `redwoodctl route set --tenant acme-tooling --concurrency 8` -> success.
Oliver: also applied fallback model variant: `redwoodctl model route --tenant acme-tooling --model rwd-xxl-fixedkernel-v2 --policy force-kernel=long_seq` -> success.
Maya: thanks. monitoring shows p95 improving already from ~800ms to ~260ms after routing change :thumbsup:
Cheng: long term we should adjust batching heuristic to incorporate nested tool-call patterns and prefer kernel stability over marginal throughput gains when eviction churn is high. I'll open a design doc/PR.
Sarah: created incident ticket and linked to perf graphs: https://incidents/redwood/INC-2026-2123
Aisha: note to infra: we should consider per-tenant kvcache reservation or soft pinning to avoid eviction storms caused by long/short interleaving
Oliver: small follow-up — can we add a short-lived trace sampling for that tenant to catch recurrence?
perf-bot: sampling rule added: tenant acme-tooling -> sample rate 1.0 for 2h
Maya: closing loop: if p95 stays <300ms for next 30m we can roll back routing changes and keep config fixes queued. great quick work team :fire:
Aisha: will follow up with a postmortem draft and suggested mitigation list (kvcache reservation, batching-weight smoothing, prefetch stability metric)
Maya: assign owners when draft is ready. thanks everyone.
